matches.title: Osasuna vs Barcelona
matches.description: Watch Osasuna vs Barcelona highlights and goals from La Liga on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 2, 2026. Under the floodlights on May 2, 2026 , Barcelona traveled to face a resilient Osasuna side in a La Liga encounter that promised tactical intrigue. Both sides looked to impose their rhythm in a contest where every inch of turf was fiercely contested from the opening whistle. A Cagey Opening at El Sadar The first half was characterized by Barcelona ’s trademark territorial dominance, as the Catalan giants controlled 70% of the possession but struggled to find a clinical edge. Dani Olmo and Roony Bardghji were active in the early stages, frequently looking to exploit the flanks and delivering several corners, yet the Osasuna defense remained disciplined. The hosts were content to absorb pressure, leading to a string of goal kicks as the final ball from the visitors often lacked the necessary precision to trouble the goalkeeper. Despite the pressure from the visitors, it was Osasuna who came closest to breaking the deadlock in the 37th minute. Ante Budimir found himself with a golden opportunity to put the home side ahead, but his well-struck effort rattled against the post and stayed out. It was a massive let-off for Barcelona , who had dictated the tempo but lacked the bite to match their aesthetic buildup play. The half ended goalless, with Gavi picking up a yellow card as the physical nature of the contest began to ramp up. Tactical Adjustments and the Breakthrough The second half saw the intensity increase as both managers looked to their benches to find a solution. After Eric Garcia was cautioned for a tactical foul at the hour mark, Barcelona boss Hansi Flick opted for a triple substitution, introducing Marcus Rashford , Ferran Torres , and Frenkie de Jong . These changes injected immediate pace and directness into the Blaugrana attack, forcing Osasuna deeper into their own territory. The deadlock was finally broken in the 81st minute. Marcus Rashford , making an immediate impact, delivered a pinpoint cross into the heart of the box where Robert Lewandowski was waiting. The veteran striker rose highest to power a header home, finally giving Barcelona the lead they had craved. Just five minutes later, the visitors seemed to have put the game to bed. Fermin Lopez turned provider, finding Ferran Torres in space, and the Spanish international made no mistake with a sharp right-footed finish to make it 2-0. Late Drama and a Frantic Finish However, Osasuna refused to surrender. Just two minutes after Barcelona ’s second goal, the home side struck back to set up a grandstand finish. Substitute Abel Bretones swung in a dangerous cross that was met by Raul Garcia , whose header flew into the net to make it 2-1 in the 88th minute. The goal breathed new life into El Sadar, as the home fans rallied behind their team for one final push. The closing minutes were frantic and filled with missed opportunities at both ends. Ferran Torres had a chance to restore the two-goal cushion but uncharacteristically fired wide from a position he would usually convert. At the other end, Flavien Boyomo saw a header go agonizingly wide for the hosts during a period of sustained aerial bombardment. As tensions boiled over in the ninth minute of stoppage time, Enrique Barja was shown a yellow card for dissent, but the referee soon blew the final whistle to confirm a hard-fought victory for Barcelona .

matches.title: Valencia vs Barcelona
matches.description: Watch Valencia vs Barcelona highlights and goals from La Liga on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 23, 2026. The clash between Valencia and Barcelona promised a high-stakes tactical battle in the heart of La Liga . With both sides eager to claim dominance, the atmosphere was electric as the teams prepared for a decisive encounter. Tactical Stalemate and Possession Play On 23 May 2026 , Barcelona arrived with a clear intent to control the tempo, maintaining a staggering 76% of possession throughout the match. The first half saw the visitors dominate the ball, with Marcus Rashford delivering several dangerous corners to test the home defense. Valencia , however, remained disciplined despite an early scare involving a defensive blunder by Javier Guerra . While the territorial advantage belonged to the Catalan giants, clear-cut opportunities were scarce, and both teams headed into the tunnel with the scoreline still untouched. The Breakthrough and a Rapid Response The game truly ignited in the second half. In the 61st minute, Barcelona finally broke the deadlock when Ferran Torres provided a pinpoint assist for Robert Lewandowski , who finished clinically with his left foot. The lead, however, was fleeting. Just five minutes later, Javier Guerra made amends for his earlier error by firing home the equalizer. The momentum swung violently in favor of the hosts, and by the 71st minute, Luis Rioja pounced on a loose ball to strike with his left foot, completing a swift turnaround that left the visitors stunned. VAR Drama and the Final Blow The final stages of the match were defined by tension and VAR intervention. In the 77th minute, the referee initially awarded a penalty to Valencia after a foul by Marc Bernal , only to revoke the decision after a lengthy video review. Barcelona pushed for a late equalizer, with Andreas Christensen seeing a powerful header saved by Stole Dimitrievski , but the hosts had the final word. In the 7th minute of stoppage time, Guido Rodriguez unleashed a thunderous strike from outside the box to seal a 3-1 victory, capping off an incredible second-half performance for Valencia .

The stage was set for a classic encounter as two ambitious sides prepared to leave their mark on the pitch. This La Liga showdown took place on May 17, 2026, pitting Barcelona against Real Betis in a high-stakes tactical battle. Raphinha’s early brilliance The Barcelona attack looked sharp from the opening whistle, consistently testing the opposition's defensive line. The breakthrough arrived in the 28th minute when Raphinha stepped up to a free kick, curling a precise left-footed effort into the net. While Real Betis looked to find a way back into the match, they struggled to bypass a resilient home defense, even as Jules Koundé was cautioned for his defensive work. Second-half drama and tactical shifts Momentum shifted early in the second half when Raphinha doubled the lead in the 62nd minute, capitalizing on a defensive error by Hector Bellerin . However, the tide turned when Isco entered the fray. Following a tense VAR intervention, a penalty was awarded for a foul by Gavi , which Isco coolly converted in the 69th minute. The goal breathed new life into the visitors, creating a nervous atmosphere for the home faithful. Cancelo seals the deal Despite the pressure, Barcelona regained control through fresh legs off the bench. In the 74th minute, Joao Cancelo hammered home a right-footed strike from outside the box, assisted by Pedri , effectively extinguishing any hope of a comeback. The final minutes saw Barcelona manage the game effectively, holding onto their lead to secure three important points.

matches.title: Deportivo Alavés vs Barcelona
matches.description: Watch Deportivo Alavés vs Barcelona highlights and goals from La Liga on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 13, 2026. The stage was set at Mendizorroza on May 13, 2026 , as Deportivo Alavés hosted Barcelona in a high-stakes La Liga encounter. Both teams took to the pitch with contrasting philosophies, setting the scene for a tactical battle that would keep the fans on the edge of their seats. Diabate Strikes Before the Break From the opening whistle, Barcelona established their dominance in possession, eventually controlling 77% of the ball. However, despite their territorial advantage, the visitors struggled to find a clinical finishing touch. Roony Bardghji was a frequent threat from corner situations, but his deliveries often failed to connect with a teammate. Deportivo Alavés , meanwhile, remained disciplined and dangerous on the counter-attack, with Denis Suarez delivering several testing corners that kept the Catalan defense on high alert. The deadlock was finally broken in the first minute of first-half stoppage time. Antonio Blanco provided a sublime assist to find Ibrahim Diabate , who maintained his composure to slot the ball home with his right foot. The goal at 45+1' sent the home crowd into raptures and left Barcelona searching for answers as they headed into the interval trailing by a goal. Defensive Resilience Thwarts Barcelona Barcelona emerged for the second half with increased urgency, but their frustration was evident as Marcus Rashford picked up an early yellow card. Alavés nearly doubled their lead in the 51st minute when Ibrahim Diabate saw a goalbound header comfortably saved by Wojciech Szczesny . In an attempt to turn the tide, the Barcelona bench made a triple substitution after the hour mark, introducing Pedri , Ferran Torres , and Xavi Espart to inject fresh creativity into the midfield and attack. Despite the reinforcements and relentless pressure, the Deportivo Alavés defense held firm. Ville Koski was instrumental in intercepting dangerous crosses, while goalkeeper Antonio Sivera commanded his area with confidence. As the clock wound down, the match became more physical, with Abderrahman Rebbach and Joao Cancelo receiving cautions. Even with the late introduction of Tommy Marques , Barcelona could not find a way through the resilient blue and white wall. The final whistle confirmed a significant victory for Alavés , who executed their game plan to perfection.
